experiment_data.hypothesis: Forcing d=1.0 (3PL degradation) on PSN-IRT 4PL parameters systematically distorts lz* values for real LLM response data, with the largest distortion on benchmarks/models where items have low d_feasibility, providing empirical evidence (beyond simulation) that the 4PL upper asymptote is essential for accurate person-fit measurement in LLM evaluation

metrics.bias_direction: 3PL systematically depresses high-ability models' lz* (d=1 makes P→1, amplifying few-error aberrance)
metrics.key_finding: Ignoring d parameter makes lz* completely unreliable for high-ability models — d-induced bias far exceeds any contamination signal
